thread:
Maya: Heads-up — AcmeHealth reached out asking for a reliable quant-fallback + cache hints for long-context RAG. They want guidance on latency and a fallback path if quantization degrades quality. Need to decide priority for next sprint.

Liam: +1 we need to prioritize. My gut: eval-triggered alerts first so we can detect regressions quickly. Batching/cache improvements are higher dev cost.

Neha: Agree on alerts as a fast signal. Proposed minimal flow: ingest eval set, compute metrics, fire alerts to #ops when quality drops. Then add auto-threshold tuning.

Samir: Quant-fallback is non-trivial — requires variant routing, compatibility tests, and perf baselines. Rough estimate: prototype 2-3 wks, hardening 1-2 wks.

Elen: From CS: AcmeHealth will likely stall Dedicated until they see fallback guarantees. Could we offer an "opt-in" limited MVP (only to redwood-verified model pairs) to reduce scope?

Maya: MVP proposal to discuss: 1) Eval-triggered alerts integrated with alerting + slack + ops dashboard (MUST). 2) KV/prefix cache heuristics improvements (SHOULD, low effort). 3) Quant fallback as opt-in prototype to verified model pairs (COULD). Launch criteria to gate: a) alert false-positive rate <10% on validation, b) end-to-end Sanity test against AcmeHealth sample set, c) runbook for rollback + SLOs documented.

Liam: Tradeoffs: Alerts = low dev, high organizational value. Quant-fallback = high engineering cost but high commercial value for AcmeHealth. Can we parallelize? ship alerts in sprint, start quant prototype with a single eng pair.

Samir: I can take the prototype with Neha. Plan: routing shim + simple health-check + canary. Will allocate 20% sprint for routing + 50% next sprint for validation.

Neha: I'll own eval triggers and thresholds. Need ~50 labeled prompts from AcmeHealth to tune triggers. Also propose an initial rule format: 
```
rule: eval_drop
metric: answer_f1
threshold: -6% relative
window: 1h
notify: #ops
```

Maya: @Samir @Neha please sync with @Elen on acceptance tests and compliance checklist. Also we need a quick cost delta estimate: how often fallback will spin up and expected per-token cost change.

Elen: I'll ask AcmeHealth for the labeled prompts and whether they require on-prem fallback or hosted-only. Also pulling finance for a quick unit-cost calc.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled a canary workspace for quant-proto at 2025-11-06T14:00Z — ticket #RD-1983.

Liam: Decision for sprint planning: ship eval-triggered alerts as MVP slice. Start quant prototype (Samir+Neha) in parallel as a separate sub-track. Maya to write acceptance criteria and link to the product PR by EOD Friday.

Maya: I'll draft the acceptance doc in #product and ping reviewers. Quick follow-ups: 1) Neha - list of required eval signals, 2) Samir - prototype interface sketch for routing, 3) Elen - timeline for customer prompt delivery. Thanks all.
